audit.whatIsWrong: Wither is said to shut off Ambessa's dash. It appears as 'one Wither shuts off your attack speed AND your dash', 'it cripples your attack speed and your dash' and 'Withers off your attack speed and your dash' — four places, and it is the stated reason the late game is unwinnable.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Nasus ages an enemy champion, decelerating their Move Speed and Attack Speed over time.' It is a slow on two stats. It does not ground, root or disable anything. Drakehound's Step is a dash of fixed distance triggered off her casts — a move-speed slow does not remove it. What Wither genuinely does to her is gut the attack speed her empowered auto and her whole ability-into-auto chain run on, which is bad enough to be worth saying accurately.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text, early, late, wants.foe[0] and whys[6] now say attack speed and move speed, with Wither's 15s at rank 1 and 700 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'His E shred eats your physical-only damage' — stated in late and whys[6]. Spirit Fire's shred points the other way.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Nasus unleashes a spirit flame at a location, dealing damage and reducing the Armor of enemies who stand on it.' It strips YOUR armour, making his Siphoning Strike hit you harder. It does nothing to protect him from physical damage. The player was told to fear standing in it for the wrong reason and given no reason to step off it.
audit.corrected: late and whys[6] now say the flame strips your armour and amplifies his Q, so step off it.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'His R lifesteal out-heals your burst' and 'R-lifesteals through your burst' credit the ultimate with sustain it does not have, and the entry never says what Fury of the Sands actually gives him.
audit.why: The life steal is Soul Eater, his passive, and it is on all game. Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80 at 400 range and grants 'increased Health, Attack Range, damages nearby enemies, has a reduced cooldown on Siphoning Strike, and gains bonus Armor and Magic Resistance'. Bonus armour on top of a physical-only opponent, plus a shorter Siphoning Strike, is a very different problem from lifesteal — and it means Grievous Wounds belongs on his passive, not saved for his ultimate.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, spikes[3].text, late, wants.foe[2] and whys[6] now attribute the sustain to Soul Eater and describe what R actually adds.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (P Soul Eater, R Fury of the Sands)

audit.whatIsWrong: early tells the player not to dive 'just after he hits 6 with a fresh Wither up', implying Wither arrives at 6.
audit.why: Wither is a basic ability available from level 2, and its cooldown is 15/14/13/12/11 — a laning-phase problem from the first minutes, not a level-6 one. Level 6 is when Fury of the Sands arrives, which is a different threat entirely.
audit.corrected: early now separates the two: respect Wither from level 2 onward, and treat 6 as the Fury of the Sands timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'R's passive armor pen plus on-ability healing' is given in spikes[2].text, mid, whys[4] and whys[5] as the reason Ambessa wins the extended trade.
audit.why: Riot's Public Execution text: 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival. She then slams the enemy into the ground where they take damage and are stunned.' No penetration, no healing, no passive. Ambessa does not win extended trades against a life-stealing Nasus — she wins short ones, and the entry's own advice elsewhere says so.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the suppression (a suppressed Nasus cannot cast Wither) and a Grievous Wounds call against Soul Eater.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Deny his Q stacks' is the entry's core instruction but never says what a stack requires.
audit.why: Riot's text: Siphoning Strike 'deals damage and increas[es] the power of his future Siphoning Strikes if he slays his target.' The stack is paid on the kill, not the cast — so denying the last hit denies the stack outright, and its 255 range means he has to be fully in melee to try. That is why standing on the caster minions works.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text and whys[3] now state the kill condition and the 255 range.

notes: Three mechanical inversions here, all of which change what the player does. Wither does not touch her dash — Riot's text is a move-speed and attack-speed decay — so the 'it turns your whole kit off' framing was overstated in the wrong direction; the attack-speed half is the real problem. Spirit Fire reduces the ARMOUR OF ENEMIES STANDING ON IT, so it amplifies his damage on you rather than blunting yours on him; 'his E shred eats your physical damage' was backwards. And the life steal is Soul Eater, the passive, not the ultimate — Fury of the Sands gives him health, attack range, bonus armour and MR and a shorter Siphoning Strike, which is why Grievous Wounds should be bought against the passive rather than held for 6. Public Execution's invented 'armor pen plus on-ability healing' was removed for the fourth time in this slice. DATA CONFLICT worth checking: this packet records Ambessa at 53.54% over 297 games against Nasus, while the completed mirror at audits/top/nasus__ambessa.json cites Nasus at 52.27% for the same pairing. Both cannot be right. I did not touch the level chart — the mirror auditor also found that side flips are impossible to propose, since 'Ambessa' is seven characters and 'Nasus' is five, which is a 28.6% change and outside the applier's band.
